newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids mostly edge up with crude, gas.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids mostly edge up with crude, gas.

text.p: U.S. spot fuel oil prices mostly edged higher Thursday in moderate trade, driven by firm crude, another record rally in gas and forecasts for colder East Coast weather later this week and next, sources said.

"The runup in gas has given resid sellers the courage to throw out some big numbers, but everyone has oil," said one cash trader, adding demand was just starting to pick up as weather and high gas prices boosted fuel oil burns.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent gained 25-50 cents to $22.00-25 a barrel, with December paper talked up the same amount at about $22.25, traders said.
NYH January one percent paper sold at $22.40, up more than 25 cents on the day.
High sulphurs in NYH edged up slightly, with 2.2 percent now pegged on either side of $20.50.
Bids are due Tuesday for a Midwest utility tender for 0.7 percent material for December delivery.
A New York utility tendered for 100,000 barrels of 1.5 percent for 12/20 delivery. Bids are due Friday at 1200 EST.
At the U.S. Gulf, prices were stable, with one percent still at $18.75-19.00 and three percent at $17.75-18.00.
A trader said 500,000 barrels of USG three percent sold in the $17.25-50 range but the exact price was not confirmed.
USG three percent paper was done at $18.75, up 20 cents.

New York City gate swing gas surged another 50-plus cents Thursday to the $4.50-60/mmBtu area on colder weather in the area. NYH one percent resid was at a $3.51/mmBtu equivalent. In December, New York gas remained quoted at $5.00/mmBtu or better versus resid paper at a $3.53/mmBtu equivalent.
